domains.name: Prospecting, Outreach & Pipeline Operations
domains.description: Measures the program's spine: conducting professional outreach at scale, researching and qualifying targets, crafting and testing messages, booking and running informational interviews, operating a CRM pipeline with funnel discipline, and maintaining a skills-first public presence.

domains.name: Sales Fundamentals
domains.description: Measures understanding of sales roles and metrics, discovery and qualification technique, objection handling, and reading a personal pipeline as a funnel.

domains.name: Applied AI & Automation
domains.description: Measures practical AI skill: structured prompting across leading LLMs, judging output fitness, using AI to accelerate research and personalization without losing accuracy or authenticity, and building simple workflow automations that save measurable time.

domains.name: Software Development Fundamentals
domains.description: Measures entry-level programming literacy: core concepts applied to real data tasks, understanding and calling APIs, and version control with Git and GitHub through to a published, documented script.

domains.name: Digital Marketing Fundamentals
domains.description: Measures positioning and content strategy, interpreting engagement analytics on real posts, and designing a simple campaign with a clear audience, message, channel, cadence, and metric.

domains.name: Professional Communication & Career Readiness
domains.description: Measures evidence-based pathway decision-making, synthesizing work into a portfolio and metrics story, delivering a results presentation, and managing the transition into an apprenticeship with professional assets the participant owns.

subdomains.name: Outreach fundamentals and daily routine
subdomains.description: Writing personalized connection requests and follow-ups and sustaining a daily outreach routine at quota.

subdomains.name: Target research and list building
subdomains.description: Defining ideal contact profiles, researching and qualifying prospects, and mapping multiple contacts inside priority organizations.

subdomains.name: Messaging craft and testing
subdomains.description: Testing message variants against real reply data and adapting tone and ask to the audience.

subdomains.name: Informational interviews
subdomains.description: Converting replies into scheduled conversations and conducting structured informational interviews with useful debriefs.

subdomains.name: CRM and pipeline operations
subdomains.description: Operating a live prospecting pipeline in an industry-standard CRM: stages, prioritization, funnel metrics, and follow-up discipline.

subdomains.name: Personal brand and public presence
subdomains.description: Maintaining a skills-first LinkedIn presence and publishing posts that support outreach goals.

subdomains.name: Sales roles and team metrics
subdomains.description: The SDR/BDR, AE, and sales engineering role landscape and how sales teams are measured.

subdomains.name: Discovery and qualification
subdomains.description: Applying a discovery framework in live conversations and scoring a pipeline against qualification criteria.

subdomains.name: Objection handling
subdomains.description: Recognizing common objections and responding in ways that keep conversations alive without being pushy.

subdomains.name: Funnel analysis and pipeline discipline
subdomains.description: Analyzing a personal pipeline as a funnel, spotting stage-conversion problems, and presenting findings.

subdomains.name: Structured prompting across LLMs
subdomains.description: Prompting Claude and ChatGPT with structure, comparing model outputs, and judging fitness for purpose.

subdomains.name: AI-assisted research and personalization
subdomains.description: Using AI to accelerate prospect research and message personalization while critiquing drafts for accuracy and authenticity.

subdomains.name: Workflow automation
subdomains.description: Designing and building a working automation that saves measurable time in a real workflow.

subdomains.name: Programming concepts through real tasks
subdomains.description: Core programming concepts — variables, functions, loops, data structures — applied to practical contact-list tasks in TypeScript.

subdomains.name: Data and APIs
subdomains.description: What APIs are and using a script to pull and transform real pipeline data.

subdomains.name: Version control and shipping
subdomains.description: Git fundamentals and publishing working code to GitHub with a plain-language README.

subdomains.name: Positioning and content strategy
subdomains.description: Crafting a positioning statement and deconstructing high-performing content into hook, structure, and call to action.

subdomains.name: Analytics and attribution
subdomains.description: Interpreting impressions and engagement on real posts and identifying what actually generated conversations.

subdomains.name: Campaign thinking
subdomains.description: Designing a simple campaign: audience, message, channel, cadence, and success metric.

subdomains.name: Pathway decision-making
subdomains.description: Evaluating pathway fit using rotation performance, reflections, interview intelligence, and coach input, and justifying the choice in writing.

subdomains.name: Portfolio and metrics storytelling
subdomains.description: Synthesizing weeks of pipeline data into a metrics story, a personal playbook, and a portfolio of best artifacts.

subdomains.name: Presentation craft
subdomains.description: Building, rehearsing, and delivering a short results presentation and giving structured peer feedback.

subdomains.name: Career transition and professional assets
subdomains.description: Apprenticeship application with portfolio evidence, resume and LinkedIn updates with real results, a 30-day transition plan, and ownership of the network and data built during the program.

competencies.statement: The learner can write a personalized connection request and follow-up sequence tailored to a specific contact.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by selecting or composing outreach messages that reference the contact's context and make a clear, low-friction ask, rather than generic blasts.

competencies.statement: The learner can execute and sustain a daily outreach routine at quota with disciplined follow-up timing.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by sequencing a daily send/follow-up/log routine and choosing appropriate follow-up cadence when contacts do not reply.

competencies.statement: The learner can define an ideal contact profile and qualify prospects against it.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by distinguishing high-fit from low-fit prospects using role, company, and relevance criteria before spending outreach effort.

competencies.statement: The learner can map multiple contacts inside a priority organization to build redundancy into an account.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by identifying 2-3 relevant roles inside a target employer and explaining why multi-threading an account beats a single contact.

competencies.statement: The learner can test message variants against real reply data and keep the better performer.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by setting up a simple A/B comparison, reading reply-rate evidence correctly, and avoiding conclusions from tiny samples.

competencies.statement: The learner can adapt message tone and ask to different audiences.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by matching formality, length, and the size of the ask to the recipient's seniority and relationship stage.

competencies.statement: The learner can convert a positive reply into a scheduled conversation.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by responding to interest with concrete times, a calendar link, and a confirmed meeting rather than an open-ended thread.

competencies.statement: The learner can conduct a structured 20-minute informational interview and debrief it usefully.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by ordering an interview's phases (rapport, prepared questions, insight capture, next-step ask, thank-you) and extracting actionable intelligence afterward.

competencies.statement: The learner can operate a CRM pipeline: stage contacts correctly and prioritize the next action.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by placing contacts in the right funnel stage, flagging priority accounts, and choosing the highest-value next activity from a working pipeline.

competencies.statement: The learner can read basic funnel metrics from a CRM and act on them.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by interpreting counts and conversion between stages and identifying where follow-up discipline is slipping.

competencies.statement: The learner can maintain a skills-first public profile that supports active outreach.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by choosing profile content that leads with demonstrable skills and work products, aligned with the outreach the contact will receive.

competencies.statement: The learner can publish public posts that reinforce outreach goals.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by selecting post topics and timing that give prospects evidence of skill and momentum when they check the sender's profile.

competencies.statement: The learner can distinguish SDR/BDR, AE, and sales engineering roles and what each is responsible for.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by matching responsibilities like prospecting, closing, and technical validation to the correct role.

competencies.statement: The learner can explain how sales teams are measured and how metrics shape behavior.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by relating metrics such as meetings booked, pipeline created, and quota attainment to the role that owns them.

competencies.statement: The learner can apply a discovery framework to structure a qualification conversation.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by choosing open discovery questions that surface need, authority, and timing rather than pitching features.

competencies.statement: The learner can score pipeline contacts against qualification criteria.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by applying explicit criteria to decide which conversations deserve continued investment and which should be deprioritized.

competencies.statement: The learner can respond to common objections in ways that keep the conversation alive.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by selecting responses that acknowledge, explore, and reframe objections such as no-time, no-budget, or send-me-an-email.

competencies.statement: The learner can analyze a personal pipeline as a funnel and identify the weakest conversion stage.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by computing stage-to-stage conversion from raw counts and locating where prospects stall.

competencies.statement: The learner can present funnel findings and a corrective plan.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by pairing an observed funnel weakness with a plausible corrective action, such as changing messaging at the stalled stage.

competencies.statement: The learner can write a structured prompt with role, context, task, and output format.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by composing or selecting prompts whose structure reliably produces the intended output versus vague single-line asks.

competencies.statement: The learner can compare outputs across models and judge fitness for purpose.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by evaluating two model responses against task requirements and choosing based on accuracy and fit rather than fluency alone.

competencies.statement: The learner can use AI to accelerate prospect research and message personalization.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by choosing effective AI workflows for research summarization and draft personalization that save time over manual work.

competencies.statement: The learner can critique AI-drafted outreach for accuracy and authenticity before sending.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by catching fabricated details, generic filler, and off-tone phrasing in AI drafts and knowing what must be verified.

competencies.statement: The learner can identify a repetitive workflow step worth automating.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by selecting automation candidates by frequency, time cost, and rule-based repeatability.

competencies.statement: The learner can design a simple automation and estimate the time it saves.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by decomposing a workflow into trigger, steps, and output, and producing a defensible time-saved estimate.

competencies.statement: The learner can apply variables, functions, loops, and basic data structures to a practical data task.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by reading or completing short TypeScript snippets that filter, count, or transform contact-list data.

competencies.statement: The learner can trace what a short program does and predict its output.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by stepping through simple control flow and array operations without running the code.

competencies.statement: The learner can explain what an API is and what a request/response exchange contains.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by identifying the roles of endpoint, request, response, and status in plain terms.

competencies.statement: The learner can use a script to pull and transform data from a source such as a CRM export.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by ordering fetch-parse-transform-output steps and recognizing what a given transformation does to real records.

competencies.statement: The learner can use Git fundamentals to save and share work in versioned steps.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by sequencing init/add/commit/push correctly and explaining what a commit represents.

competencies.statement: The learner can publish working code to GitHub with a plain-language README.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by identifying what a README must contain for a non-expert to understand and run the project.

competencies.statement: The learner can craft a positioning statement for a specific audience.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by selecting or composing statements that name the audience, the value offered, and the differentiator without jargon.

competencies.statement: The learner can deconstruct high-performing content into hook, structure, and call to action.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by identifying which element of a post drives attention, retention, and response, and why.

competencies.statement: The learner can interpret impressions and engagement metrics on real posts.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by reading a set of post metrics and distinguishing reach from engagement from conversation-generating performance.

competencies.statement: The learner can attribute outcomes to content and identify what actually generated conversations.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by connecting replies and booked meetings back to the content or activity that caused them, resisting vanity-metric conclusions.

competencies.statement: The learner can design a simple campaign with audience, message, channel, cadence, and metric.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by assembling a coherent mini-campaign plan where each element supports a stated goal such as event turnout.

competencies.statement: The learner can evaluate pathway fit using evidence from rotations, reflections, and coach input.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by weighing performance signals against preference and market evidence rather than choosing on enthusiasm alone.

competencies.statement: The learner can justify a pathway choice in writing with specific evidence.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by recognizing a well-evidenced justification versus one built on generic claims.

competencies.statement: The learner can synthesize weeks of pipeline data into a coherent metrics story.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by selecting the metrics and narrative arc that honestly represent effort, learning, and results over time.

competencies.statement: The learner can assemble a portfolio of best artifacts with a personal playbook.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by choosing artifacts that evidence each claimed skill and documenting a repeatable personal process.

competencies.statement: The learner can structure a short results presentation for a mixed audience.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by ordering problem, approach, evidence, and ask for a 7-10 minute presentation to staff and employer partners.

competencies.statement: The learner can give and use structured peer feedback to improve a presentation.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by applying specific, actionable feedback criteria rather than generic praise or criticism.

competencies.statement: The learner can update professional assets — resume and LinkedIn — with real, verifiable results.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by converting program outcomes into concrete, quantified statements a recruiter can check.

competencies.statement: The learner can build a 30-day transition plan into an apprenticeship.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by sequencing application, network follow-up, and skill-maintenance actions with realistic milestones.

competencies.statement: The learner can verify ownership and portability of the network and data built during the program.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by knowing what to export and retain — CRM data, LinkedIn connections, content — so the professional network remains theirs.
